items.summary: This study aims to interpret the Prophetic hadiths related to mental health and examine their relevance to modern neuropsychology. items.title: James Thomas Fitzsimons
items.summary: Abstract Photograph of James Fitzsimons. James Fitzsimons was a scientific giant, a revered colleague and a charismatic leader. He discovered the physiological basis of thirst and sodium appetite, and the neural control for their perception. His work provided a conceptual shift by showing that peptides are not just hormones in the blood but can act as signalling molecules that can act directly in the brain to regulate behaviour and physiology, fundamentally changing our understanding of neuroscience. He was an inspirational lecturer in the Physiological Laboratory at the University of Cambridg

items.summary: Non-neuronal cells do not simply detect neuronal activity; they can regulate neuronal plasticity and behaviour. One way these cells regulate neuronal plasticity is by removing synapses. For example, microglia clear synapses during development and disease through complement-dependent and independent mechanisms (Pereira-Iglesias et al., 2025). items.summary: Abstract Neurotechnology-derived data faces increasing challenges due to the lack of salient policy and regulatory guidance. FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

items.title: Image processing with ImageJ
items.summary: Wayne Rasband of NIH has created ImageJ, an open source Java-written program that is now at version 1.31 and is used for many imaging applications, including those that that span the gamut from skin analysis to neuroscience. ImageJ is in the public domain and runs on any operating system (OS). ImageJ is easy to use and can do many imaging manipulations. A very large and knowledgeable group makes up the user community for ImageJ. items.title: Emotion Circuits in the Brain
items.summary: The field of neuroscience has, after a long period of looking the other way, again embraced emotion as an important research area.
